en: to be close; to be intimate

examples.en: Health and sleep are closely related.
The two countries are closely tied economically.

examples.ko: 환경과 우리 생활은 밀접하게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The environment and our daily lives are closely connected.

examples.ko: 음식과 날씨는 서로 밀접해서 계절마다 먹는 게 달라요.
examples.en: Food and weather are closely linked, so what we eat changes by season.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 밀접하다고 하는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news saying the two incidents are closely connected.

examples.ko: 이 과목은 실제 생활과 밀접하니까 재미있어요.
examples.en: This subject is closely tied to real life, so it's fun.

explain: '가깝다'는 거리나 사이 모두에 쓰지만 밀접하다는 관계나 연관이 깊을 때 써요. '밀접한 관계'처럼 거의 추상적인 것에 쓰고, 눈에 보이는 거리에는 쓰지 않아요. 보통 '~와/과 밀접하다' 형태예요.
explain_en: 가깝다 covers both distance and relationships, but 밀접하다 is for a deep relationship or connection. It is used for abstract things, as in '밀접한 관계', not for physical distance you can see. It usually takes the pattern '~와/과 밀접하다'.

examples.en: The balloon went pop.
I gave the ball a big kick and it flew far.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 앞 유리에 구멍이 뻥 뚫렸어요.
examples.en: A big hole was punched in the windshield because of the accident.
The bottle cap came off with a pop.

examples.ko: 감기가 나아서 막혔던 코가 뻥 뚫렸어요.
examples.en: My cold got better and my blocked nose cleared right up.

examples.ko: 타이어가 뻥 터지는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by the bang of the tire bursting.

explain: 무엇이 터지거나 구멍이 크게 뚫리는 소리와 모양을 한꺼번에 나타내요. '뻥 차다'처럼 힘껏 차는 모습에도 쓰고, '뻥 뚫리다'처럼 막힌 곳이 시원하게 열리는 느낌에도 써요.

phrases.en: You're making that up again, right?
phrases.nuance_ko: 과장하거나 거짓말을 할 때 친구 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요. 어른이나 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used among friends for exaggerating or lying. Do not use it with adults or superiors.

explain_en: It describes both the sound and the look of something bursting or a big hole being punched through. It is used for a hard kick, as in '뻥 차다', and for a blockage clearing with relief, as in '뻥 뚫리다'.

en: to be this way; to be like this

examples.en: If you do it this way, the lid opens easily.
I've never seen a puppy this tiny.
I can't believe things turned out like this.
My room is like this, but it's cozy and I like it.

examples.ko: 지금 상황이 요렇더라도 포기하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Even if the situation is like this, I won't give up.

examples.ko: 요렇게 비가 오는데 꼭 나가야 해요?
examples.en: Do we really have to go out when it's raining like this?

explain: '이렇다'의 작은말이에요. 대부분 '요렇게' 꼴로 쓰고, 'ㅎ 불규칙'이라 '요래요', '요런'으로 바뀌어요. 친한 사이에서 쓰는 가벼운 말투이고, 격식 있게는 '이렇다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the small form of '이렇다'. It mostly appears as '요렇게', and as an ㅎ-irregular it becomes '요래요' and '요런'. It has a light tone for close relationships; use '이렇다' when being formal.

examples.ko: 새 앱의 유용성을 직접 써 보고 판단해 보세요.
examples.en: Try the new app yourself and judge how useful it is.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 유용성이 높아서 많은 학생이 써요.
examples.en: This method is very useful, so many students use it.

examples.ko: 책의 유용성은 읽는 사람에 따라 달라요.
examples.en: How useful a book is depends on the reader.
The research results were recognized in terms of usefulness.

examples.ko: 광고에서는 제품의 유용성보다 디자인을 먼저 보여 줘요.
examples.en: Ads show the design first rather than how useful the product is.

examples.ko: 이 기능의 유용성에 대해 회의에서 이야기했어요.
examples.en: We talked about how useful this feature is in the meeting.

explain: '유용하다'를 명사로 만든 말이고 '유용성이 높다/낮다', '유용성을 검증하다'처럼 평가하는 말과 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '쓸모', '도움이 되는 정도'라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of '유용하다' and pairs well with evaluating words, as in '유용성이 높다/낮다' and '유용성을 검증하다'. In daily talk people often say '쓸모' or '도움이 되는 정도' instead.

examples.en: This book is exactly what beginners need.
Now is precisely the time to start.
Health is the greatest asset of all.
Promises, above all, are what you must keep.
Hangul is truly Korea's pride.
My classmates are truly the best team.

explain: '이야말로'는 여러 가운데 '바로 이것'이라고 강조하는 조사예요. 받침이 있는 말 뒤에는 '이야말로', 없는 말 뒤에는 '야말로'를 써요: '지금이야말로', '너야말로'. 상대의 인사를 받아서 '저야말로요'라고 하면 '오히려 제가 그래요'라는 대답이 돼요.
explain_en: '이야말로' is a particle that stresses 'this very one' among many. After a final consonant use '이야말로', and after a vowel use '야말로', as in '지금이야말로' and '너야말로'. In reply to someone, '저야말로요' means 'if anything, it's me'.
